To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the UGIS is a promising tool for supporting curriculum mapping and that the UGIS acceptance is influenced by the unit conveners’ and academics’ perceived usefulness, perceived easiness of use and their attitude towards the UGIS.
the integration of social influence, self-efficacy and anxiety as additional constructs from the basic TAM improved the model fit and explained 60% of variance in the intention to use UGIS.

the integration of social influence, anxiety, and self-efficacy into the basic TAM model improves the predictive power of the model for explaining the intention of unit conveners and unit coordinators to use a unit guide information system (UGIS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a UGIS and the factors that influence academics and unit convenors in the use of UGIS to support the complex activity and process of curriculum mapping and unit guides.
the acceptance of a technology tool that supports curriculum mapping.
how the use of UGIS may be improved to better meet the needs of academics and unit convener users, and how this might contribute to the overall quality of the curriculum and the student experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has provided a model for the use of UGISs in the Australian context and that this model has a high degree of explanatory power.
the proposed model provides a good fit to the data and explains 68% of the intention to use the unit guide information system by academics and unit convenors.
UGISs can be a valuable and effective tool to support curriculum mapping and the development of unit guides in higher education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study has provided a model for understanding the acceptance of UGI systems by academics and unit convenors and has provided a basis for further work in this area.
the UGIS is a tool to support the curriculum mapping process.
this paper provides an empirical study that examines the acceptance and use intention of unit guide tools by unit conveners.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of unit guides is influenced by both personal and contextual factors and that a better understanding of the factors that impact the use of unit guide tools can help institutions better design, implement and support the use of unit and course guide tools.
unit guide systems should be easy-to-use and perceived as useful to the users.

the UGIS is a useful tool for curriculum mapping, and that its acceptance is influenced by both individual (self-efficacy, social influence, and anxiety) and system factors (perceived ease of use and usefulness).
